about: Relay satellites that may carry a lander's data to Earth, with their launch status, and real lunar orbiters used only to check the pass calculation. A relay's contribution is worked out only from a published or entered orbit, and is shown as a range 'if it flies as planned'. Queqiao-2 is not listed: it publishes no orbit a CLPS mission could book.

sources.title: Lunar Pathfinder Service Guide V004, section 3.4.2 (August 2022)

inclination_deg.reason: ESA's slides give 46.8 deg; SSTL's official Service Guide V004 gives 54.856 deg (rounded to 54.9 deg in the supplier paper). The guide calls this an indicative baseline, subject to change, and does not identify its reference plane or epoch. The discrepancy remains unresolved: both ends are swept and the central value is their middle.

arg_periapsis_deg.reason: SSTL's Service Guide V004 publishes an indicative baseline argument of pericenter of 86.322 deg. Its reference frame and epoch are not specified, and the operational orbit can change. Retain the 85 to 95 deg sensitivity range and its central 90 deg assumption; do not present it as an unpublished or confirmed operational element.

period_h.reason: Calculated from ESA's perilune and apolune heights by Kepler's third law (Moon GM from DE440): 10.84 h. ESA's slides round it to 10 h; the supplier paper gives about 10.8 h. This is a derived planning value, not an operational ephemeris.

notes: ESA's Lunar Pathfinder/Moonlight slides were downloaded through the browser on 2026-10-01 (SHA-256 01358401e32fc50695b43a26636178cb29de8dbce153bf69e71ea12ed97b8691). Page 1 was extracted and visually inspected: perilune 673.4 km, apolune 7331.8 km, inclination 46.8 deg and stated period 10 h. Its 2025 launch dates are historical. Local source: data/validation/external-sources/esa-moonlight-lunar-pathfinder.pdf.

SSTL's official Service Guide V004 was downloaded and page 22 visually inspected on 2026-10-01 (SHA-256 9c8b1be07ac6af6e0a4bcf86af59c8f13ec9161e55681413b9a235843cd9ddddf). Table in section 3.4.2: semi-major axis 5740 km, peri/aposelene 673/7331 km, eccentricity 0.58, inclination 54.856 deg, RAAN 0 deg, argument of pericenter 86.322 deg. The guide describes an indicative baseline that may change, without a reference plane or epoch. The supplier paper corroborates the rounded 54.9/86.3 deg figures; the ESA inclination discrepancy remains unresolved. Local source: data/validation/external-sources/sstl-lunar-pathfinder-service-guide-v004.pdf. Numerical simulation assumptions are retained pending an operational ephemeris.
records.name: Lunar Pathfinder
records.operator: ESA, built and operated by Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd
records.launch_note: To fly on Firefly's Blue Ghost Mission 2, integrated into its Elytra Dark orbital vehicle. ESA: launch not earlier than November 2026; SSTL: due to launch 2027.
records.orbit_note: An indicative elliptical lunar frozen orbit favouring the Southern Lunar Hemisphere. Heights use ESA's slides; SSTL Service Guide V004 supplies baseline RAAN 0 deg and argument of pericenter 86.322 deg, without a frame or epoch. Operational node and phase are not established, so both are swept. The conflicting published inclinations remain a sensitivity range.

periapsis_km.reason: Altus-1's orbit is not published (NASA: deployed 'in lunar orbit'). Assumed to be one of the five elliptical frozen orbits of NASA's reference design for the lunar relay constellation (LCRNS 3.1, Table 1, Moon principal-axis frame), whose final design belongs to Intuitive Machines under its Near Space Network contract; the range covers all five.

records.name: Altus-1 data-relay satellite
records.launch_note: Planned to fly alongside IM-3 (NASA, August 2026).
records.orbit_note: NASA says only that Altus-1 is deployed 'in lunar orbit'. The orbit used here is assumed from NASA's reference design; where its node and its place along the orbit will be is swept.

sources.title: Intuitive Machines Selects SpaceX to Launch its Fourth Lunar Lander Mission and Lunar Data Relay Satellites (press release, 8 April 2025)

notes: The release names neither of the two satellites: this record and the next are this project's labels for them, first and second of two, not the company's names.

Intuitive Machines' own copies of the release did not load when this was compiled (its investor page timed out twice and refused a plain request with 403, and its news page needs a browser to show any text), so the release was read as Intuitive Machines distributed it through GlobeNewswire.

No orbit is assumed. Altus-1's record assumes one of the five frozen orbits of NASA's reference design, but two relays given that same assumption would be swept at the same place and counted as one; which of the five these two take is not stated.

records.orbit_note: Intuitive Machines' release gives no orbit for these satellites.
